cards.text: Jacob is still on the road to Haran to find his uncle Laban, his mother's brother (Genesis 28:2, 10). He reaches the land of the people of the east and spots a well in a field, with three flocks of sheep lying near it. A large stone covers the mouth of that well.

cards.question: A big stone sits over the well in that field. When do the shepherds roll it away to water the sheep?

answers.text: Once all the flocks are gathered there
Once the sun starts to go down
Once each shepherd pays the owner

cards.text: Jacob walks up to the shepherds by the well. "My brothers," Jacob asks the shepherds, "where are you from?"

cards.question: Jacob is headed to his uncle in Haran. Where do these shepherds at the well say they're from?

cards.text: HARAN! Out of everybody in the east, Jacob asks the shepherds from the exact town he's headed to. I once spent a whole morning hunting for my timer, and it was hanging on my APRON.

cards.question: Jacob asks the shepherds if they know Laban, the grandson of Abraham's brother Nahor. True or false: the shepherds have never heard of Laban.
Jacob asks if Laban is well. The shepherds say yes, and then they point out someone coming with Laban's sheep. Who is it?

cards.text: It's still broad daylight, so Jacob tells the shepherds, "Water the sheep and take them back to pasture." He JUST met these guys, and he's already running the well.

cards.question: Jacob tells the shepherds to water their sheep right now. What do the shepherds tell him?

answers.text: They can't until all the flocks are gathered
They already watered them this morning
They have to wait for Laban's permission

cards.text: While Jacob is still talking, Rachel arrives with her father's sheep, because she's a shepherdess.

cards.question: The shepherds won't move the stone off the well until every flock shows up. As soon as Jacob sees Rachel with Laban's sheep, what does Jacob do?

answers.text: Rolls the stone away and waters the sheep
Waits with the shepherds for the other flocks
Asks the shepherds to move it for her

cards.text: The shepherds' big rule about the stone? Jacob just ROLLS right past it. Then Jacob kisses Rachel and weeps aloud.

cards.question: Rachel just met this man at the well. What does Jacob tell her about himself?

answers.text: He's Rebekah's son and her father's relative
He's a shepherd from the east looking for work
He's a servant sent here by Abraham

cards.question: Rachel runs and tells her father that his sister's son Jacob is here. True or false: Laban waits at home for Jacob to come to him.

cards.text: Laban runs out to meet Jacob, embraces him, kisses him and brings him home. Jacob tells him all that had happened.

cards.question: After Jacob tells Laban all that had happened, what does Laban call Jacob?

answers.text: A hired hand for his flocks

cards.text: And Jacob stays with Laban for a month. A whole month with family, friend? After my years in a junk drawer, that sounds like a VACATION.
Jacob is settled in at his uncle Laban's place. Then Laban says to him, "Just because you are my relative, should you work for nothing?"

cards.question: Laban doesn't want Jacob working for nothing. So what does Laban ask Jacob to tell him?

answers.text: When he plans to go home
Why he left his father's house

cards.text: Now, Laban has two daughters, Leah and Rachel. Remember those names, friend. You're gonna NEED them.

cards.question: Laban has two daughters, Leah and Rachel. True or false: Leah is the older one.

cards.text: The text says Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful. And Jacob loves Rachel.

cards.question: Jacob loves Laban's daughter Rachel, and Laban just asked him to name his wages. What does Jacob offer Laban?

answers.text: Seven years of work for Rachel
Three years of work for Rachel
A bride price in silver for Rachel

cards.question: Laban agrees: "Stay here with me." So Jacob serves seven years for Rachel. How do those seven years feel to Jacob?

cards.text: SEVEN YEARS, and to Jacob it feels like a few days, because of his love for her. Friend, I can't wait seven MINUTES for a batch to cool without sneaking one.
Then Jacob tells Laban, "Grant me my wife, for my time is complete…" So Laban invites all the men of that place and prepares a feast.

cards.question: Laban has thrown a feast for the wedding. True or false: when evening comes, Laban gives his daughter Rachel to Jacob.

cards.text: Laban gives Jacob his daughter Leah, and gives his servant girl Zilpah to Leah as her maidservant. Then morning comes, and… "there was Leah!"

cards.question: Jacob goes straight to Laban: "Wasn't it for Rachel that I served you?" According to Jacob, what has Laban done to him?
Laban answers that it's not their custom here to give the ___ daughter in marriage before the ___ one.

cards.text: NOW we hear about the custom? Seven years and a wedding feast later? That's the fine print showing up AFTER you sign!

cards.question: Laban tells Jacob to finish this week's celebration, and then Rachel can be his wife too. What will Rachel cost Jacob this time?
Laban offers Rachel for another seven years of work. True or false: Jacob turns the deal down and heads back home.

cards.text: Jacob finishes the week's celebration, and Laban gives him Rachel as his wife. Laban also gives his servant girl Bilhah to Rachel as her maidservant.

cards.question: Jacob is married to both of Laban's daughters now. Which one does Jacob love more?

answers.text: Neither one more than the other

cards.text: So Jacob works for Laban another seven years, and I thought MY wait in that junk drawer was long! Hang on, friend, because this family's story is just getting started.

findings.problem: Card 1 says Jacob is on the road to Haran, and this question repeats that he is headed to his uncle in Haran. Then it asks where the shepherds are from, with Haran as an answer. The setup names the right answer, so the baker picks it because it was just mentioned, not by reasoning. Bethel and Beersheba never get a fair chance.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Jacob walks up and right away meets shepherds from the exact town he is looking for. That is a lucky find on the first try. The comparison is spending a whole morning hunting for a timer that was on his apron all along. That is a long search for something that was never lost, so the action doesn't match and the joke doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question calls Nahor 'Abraham's brother.' That fact comes from outside the passage (Genesis 29:5 says only 'Laban the grandson of Nahor'), and the card gives no reference for it, such as Genesis 11:26.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Genesis 29:8 is the shepherds repeating the custom already stated in 29:3, and card 2 already asked about it. Both cards have the same right answer (wait until all the flocks are gathered). The repeated line is asked a second time.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The question asks how the seven years felt in length. 'Like only a few days' and 'Like they'll never end' are about time, but 'Like a hard bargain' is a judgment of the deal. It is not the same kind of answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card carries three separate things: Laban gives Leah to Jacob, Laban gives Zilpah to Leah as her maidservant, and the morning reveal 'there was Leah!'

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: 'Robbed him' is close to the right answer. Laban took seven years of Jacob's work and kept back the bride he worked for, so a baker could argue that Jacob was robbed.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Two answers are single names (Rachel, Leah) and the third is a long phrase ('Neither one more than the other'). The answers are not about the same length or the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
